summary: Peginterferon alfa-2a (pegylated interferon alpha-2a) is a long-acting interferon used for chronic hepatitis C (alone or, classically, in combination with ribavirin and/or direct-acting antivirals) and for chronic hepatitis B (HBeAg-positive and HBeAg-negative). It is a conjugate of interferon alfa-2a with polyethylene glycol, which slows clearance and allows once-weekly subcutaneous dosing at 180 micrograms. Interferon binds type I interferon receptors and induces antiviral and immunomodulatory effects. It carries a BOXED WARNING that alpha interferons may cause or aggravate fatal or life-threatening neuropsychiatric (depression, suicidal ideation), autoimmune, ischemic, and infectious disorders; patients must be monitored closely and treatment stopped for severe reactions. When combined with ribavirin, additional boxed warnings apply (ribavirin causes hemolytic anemia and is teratogenic/embryocidal - pregnancy must be avoided). Dose reductions are needed for cytopenias and renal/hepatic effects, and it is contraindicated in autoimmune hepatitis and decompensated liver disease.
indications: Chronic hepatitis C in adults (and pediatric patients per labeling), used in combination regimens with ribavirin and/or other antivirals
Chronic hepatitis B (HBeAg-positive and HBeAg-negative) with compensated liver disease and evidence of viral replication and inflammation

dosage.d: 180 micrograms subcutaneously once weekly, with weight/genotype-based ribavirin; duration 24-48 weeks by genotype
dosage.n: Combine with ribavirin (and/or DAA) per regimen; dose-reduce for adverse effects

dosage.d: 180 micrograms subcutaneously once weekly for 48 weeks
Reduce to 135 micrograms weekly (or lower, e.g., 90 micrograms) for renal impairment/hemodialysis or per-protocol cytopenias
dosage.n: Stepwise reductions for neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, depression, or other toxicity

admin: Administer by subcutaneous injection into the abdomen or thigh once weekly; rotate sites
Solution should be brought to room temperature; do not use if discolored or containing particulates; do not shake
Obtain baseline labs (CBC, liver function, thyroid, glucose) and screen for depression and eye/cardiac disease before starting
When used with ribavirin, ensure negative pregnancy test, two forms of contraception, and follow ribavirin boxed-warning precautions
Store refrigerated; patients may self-inject after appropriate training; provide a hepatitis medication guide
moa: Peginterferon alfa-2a is recombinant interferon alfa-2a covalently bound to a 40-kDa branched polyethylene glycol (PEG) molecule. Interferon alfa binds to type I interferon (IFNAR) receptors on the cell surface, activating the JAK-STAT signaling pathway and inducing transcription of numerous interferon-stimulated genes. This produces antiviral effects (inhibition of viral replication in infected cells), antiproliferative activity, and immunomodulation (enhanced macrophage phagocytosis, augmented lymphocyte cytotoxicity, and modulation of natural killer cell activity). Pegylation reduces renal clearance and proteolysis, sustaining serum concentrations and allowing effective once-weekly dosing.

absolute: Hepatic decompensation (Child-Pugh class B/C) in cirrhotic patients (and in HIV-coinfected cirrhotics with score >=6)
Neonates and infants (formulations containing benzyl alcohol)
Known severe hypersensitivity to interferon alfa or any product component
When combined with ribavirin: pregnancy and male partners of pregnant women; also ribavirin contraindications (e.g., hemoglobinopathies, severe renal impairment)
relative: History of severe psychiatric disorder (depression, suicidal ideation)
Pre-existing autoimmune disease, thyroid disease, severe cardiac or pulmonary disease, retinopathy/diabetes/hypertension
Significant cytopenias, transplant recipients (other than liver in some cases), severe renal impairment
monitor: Complete blood count (neutropenia, thrombocytopenia), liver and thyroid function, glucose
Ophthalmologic, cardiovascular, pulmonary, and autoimmune signs

preg: Peginterferon alfa-2a may cause fetal harm based on its antiproliferative/abortifacient potential in animals; use in pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the risk. When used in combination with ribavirin, the regimen is CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy and in male partners of pregnant women because ribavirin is teratogenic and embryocidal - effective contraception (two methods) is required during and for 6 months after therapy.
lact: It is not known whether peginterferon alfa-2a is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a nursing infant, a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or the drug, taking into account the importance of therapy to the mother (and ribavirin precautions if combined).
renal: Clearance is reduced in renal impairment. A reduced dose (e.g., 135 micrograms once weekly) is recommended for patients with significant renal impairment or end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, with close monitoring for adverse effects and further dose reduction if needed.
hepatic: Hepatic function may worsen during therapy; persistent or worsening hepatic decompensation requires discontinuation. It is contraindicated in autoimmune hepatitis and in decompensated cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B/C). Monitor liver function tests, and stop the drug for signs of hepatic failure.

major: Ribavirin - hemolytic anemia, teratogenicity (combination boxed warnings)
Didanosine - increased risk of hepatic decompensation, lactic acidosis, pancreatitis (avoid coadministration)
Telbivudine - increased risk of peripheral neuropathy (avoid combination)
Theophylline - peginterferon inhibits CYP1A2 and increases theophylline levels (monitor)
moderate: Methadone - interferon may increase methadone exposure (monitor for toxicity)
Myelosuppressive agents (e.g., zidovudine, chemotherapy) - additive cytopenias
CYP1A2 substrates - levels may rise due to CYP1A2 inhibition
minor: Live vaccines - reduced response/possible risk during immunomodulation
interactions.food: Not applicable (subcutaneous injection); maintain adequate hydration.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol - it accelerates liver disease progression and worsens depression.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor CBC, liver function tests, thyroid function (TSH), and blood glucose; obtain a baseline eye examination; pregnancy testing when combined with ribavirin.

common: Influenza-like symptoms (fever, chills, myalgia, headache, fatigue)
serious: Autoimmune disorders (thyroiditis, lupus-like, autoimmune hepatitis, immune thrombocytopenia)
Ischemic events (myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular events, arrhythmia)
Bone marrow suppression / severe cytopenias, aplastic anemia
Retinopathy and vision loss, pulmonary disorders (interstitial pneumonitis), pancreatitis, colitis
emergency: Suicidal ideation or acute psychiatric crisis

monitoring: Complete blood count (with differential) at baseline, week 2 and 4, then periodically (neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia)
Liver function tests, thyroid function (TSH), and blood glucose at baseline and periodically
Screen for and monitor depression, mood, and suicidal ideation throughout therapy
Baseline and periodic eye examinations; monitor cardiovascular and pulmonary status
Hepatitis B/C viral markers for treatment response; pregnancy tests when used with ribavirin
counsel: Flu-like symptoms (fever, aches, chills, tiredness) are common, especially early - taking the injection at bedtime and using acetaminophen as advised can help
This medicine can cause or worsen depression and other mood changes - tell your doctor or seek help immediately for sadness, hopelessness, or thoughts of harming yourself
Keep all blood-test appointments to check blood counts, liver, thyroid, and blood sugar; report fever or signs of infection
If you also take ribavirin, you and your partner must avoid pregnancy and use two reliable methods of birth control during and for 6 months after treatment
Avoid alcohol, learn proper injection and storage technique, and report vision changes, chest pain, severe stomach pain, or shortness of breath
pk: Serum concentrations detectable within hours; antiviral/immunologic effects build over weeks
Peak serum concentration approximately 72-96 hours after subcutaneous dose
Terminal elimination half-life approximately 80 hours (range ~50-140 hours)
Refrigerate at 2-8 C (36-46 F); do not freeze; protect from light; do not shake
pearls: BOXED WARNING: alpha interferons may cause or aggravate fatal or life-threatening NEUROPSYCHIATRIC (depression, suicidality), AUTOIMMUNE, ISCHEMIC, and INFECTIOUS disorders - monitor closely and discontinue for severe reactions
When combined with ribavirin, the regimen is contraindicated in pregnancy (ribavirin is teratogenic/embryocidal) and causes hemolytic anemia - enforce two-method contraception and monitor hemoglobin
Contraindicated in autoimmune hepatitis and decompensated cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B/C)
Pegylation gives a long half-life (~80 h) enabling once-weekly 180 microgram subcutaneous dosing; reduce dose for renal impairment and cytopenias
Inhibits CYP1A2 - monitor theophylline and other CYP1A2 substrates; avoid didanosine and telbivudine combinations
missed: If a weekly dose is missed and remembered within 1-2 days, inject it as soon as possible and resume the regular weekly schedule. If several days have passed (closer to the next dose), contact the prescriber for guidance rather than doubling the dose.
overdose: Overdoses up to several times the recommended weekly dose, including daily dosing, have been reported; effects are intensified versions of the usual adverse reactions (severe fatigue, myalgia, cytopenias, hepatic and neuropsychiatric effects). There is no specific antidote; peginterferon is not effectively removed by hemodialysis or hemofiltration. Management is supportive with close monitoring of blood counts and organ function and appropriate symptomatic treatment.
